final.verdict: The 14 balls pass at their catalog sizes. The round-2 fixes all hold: the tennis felt is clean in the Wide view and on its card, the bowling bores read dark, the 3 and 11 are red against the orange 5 and 13, and the ping-pong ball is bright white. Every silhouette sits on its physics circle (0 mm excess, baseball stitches 0.54 mm, beach valve 1.6 mm). Every item builds in 103 ms or less and has 27k triangles or fewer. The group still fails because two balls break when resized, and the radius handle and the 5 mm to 1 m diameter slider make resizing a normal action. The baseball's stitches and the beach ball's valve and seam dips are fixed millimetre sizes, so a 1 to 2.5 cm baseball is covered in fat red tubes and a 1 to 6 cm beach ball gets a valve disc wider than itself and deep pumpkin-like lobes. That is the same kind of problem as round 2's bowling-ball-at-small-sizes major. Also outside the group: the glass-marble card is still a white disc (thumbs3d.js). Method: I reused my page web/dev/r2-review-balls.html in my own built-in-browser tab (Apple M5 Pro GPU, 2048x1536 canvas; tab closed at the end). I looked at a Wide shot, a 4-view sheet per ball (context, front, side-above, macro), a frontal outline overlay of all 14, the catalog-card sheet, billiard 0/1/3/5/8/9/11/13/15, a size series (baseball 1.2/2.5/7.4/30 cm, beach 1.2/2.5/6 cm, tennis 30 cm), table-level contact shots and an isolated marble. Pictures are in web/dev/shots/r2-balls-r3-*.png. I also measured model extents at 5 mm, 2 cm, 30 cm and 1 m. Console: no WebGL, shader or 404 warnings; the only errors are the cost page's own deliberate 'cost done' throws. machines/test_rg.py: PASS. Round 1's file (scratchpad/round1/balls.json) does not exist, so I judged everything fresh.

findings.problem: The stitches and leather details are fixed absolute sizes, so any size other than 7.4 cm looks wrong: the stitch spread is lat = 0.0029 / r (line 948), and the thread radius 0.46 mm, the 0.4/0.8/0.7 mm dive offsets and the leather at r - 0.3 mm are fixed (lines 1019-1036, 1089). At 1.2 cm and 2.5 cm (shots r2-balls-r3-size-baseball0012, -0025) fat red tubes cover the ball. At 30 cm (-baseball03) they become hair-thin threads with the texture's hole dots far either side. The normal map bakes absolute heights with R = r (line 970), so the seam crease is too steep when small and vanishes when large. The maps' memo key includes r (line 967), so every new size during a radius-handle or slider drag re-bakes 1280x640 maps: 106-117 ms on the main thread per step (other balls 0-4 ms) plus about 6.6 MB of new canvases and textures that the module cache never frees.
findings.fix: Let k = r / 0.037. Make the plan size-free: lat = 0.0784 rad (0.0029 / 0.037), memo key 'baseball|plan'. Make the maps size-free: memo key `baseball|${color}` and call normalsOf(hts, W, H, 0.037, 1), so the heights stay drawn for the standard ball. In the stitch geometry, scale in plan: tubeR across the seam = 0.00046*k. Keep the outline: make the tube cross-section an ellipse with radial semi-axis min(0.00046*k, 0.0005), the proud term 0.0004*min(k,1)*sin(PI f)^0.35, the dive terms 0.0008*k and 0.0007*k, and leather at r - 0.0003*min(k,1). Then the thread top stays within about 0.6 mm of r from 5 mm to 1 m (check with the bounds probe), the default 74 mm ball is unchanged, and a resize costs about 2 ms instead of 110 ms.

findings.problem: The valve and the seam dip are fixed absolute sizes. The boss lathe is 14.4 mm across with a 4.2 mm cap at r + 1.4 mm (lines 1595-1600), and the seam dip is 1.2 mm (line 1568). At 1.2 cm and 2.5 cm (r2-balls-r3-size-beach-ball0012, -0025) the valve is a white disc wider than the ball with a black puck on top, and it sticks out of the physics outline by 4.9 mm at 5 mm and 2.2 mm at 2 cm (the limit is 2 mm, and z goes beyond d/2). The gores are cut into deep pumpkin lobes because the dip is 10-20% of r. At 6 cm (-beach-ball006) the lobes and the oversized valve are still obvious. Correct at 40 cm.
findings.fix: Let kv = Math.min(1, r / 0.2). Seam dip = 0.0012 * kv (the gaussian width stays in radians). Multiply every lathe point of the boss by kv (cache key `valve|${f6(kv)}`). Make the stem kit.cylinderY(0.0021*kv, 0.0004*kv) and place the parts at r - 0.0003*kv and r + 0.0014*kv. The default ball is unchanged; a 1 m ball keeps the real-size valve (1.6 mm proud); small balls get a proportionate valve inside the 2 mm limit.

findings.problem: The catalog card is still a white disc with the blue cat's eye floating in it (r2-balls-r3-thumbs). Cause: web/thumbs3d.js clears to alpha 0 (line 172), and three r170's transmission pass swaps a sub-1 clear alpha for white at 0.5 alpha, so the glass refracts white. The 3D view is fine.
findings.fix: web/thumbs3d.js shoot(): if any mesh in the item has material.transmission > 0, set scene.background = new THREE.Color(the card's surface colour, e.g. getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--card') || '#f4f2ee') for that render and restore null afterwards (or render it on an opaque clear in the card colour). Group-side fallback if that does not land: in balls.js patch the glass shader so that when getTransmissionSample(...).a < 0.99 it uses the studio env sampled along the refracted direction instead.

findings.problem: Up close it reads as a hollow glass bubble, not solid glass. The table and wall seen through it are barely shifted and never inverted (r2-balls-r3-marble-iso1/-iso2, -q-glass-marble), while a real 16 mm marble acts as a ball lens with an inverted, minified image. The glass sphere is also cast:false, so on a lit table the marble casts no shadow at all; a real one casts a light shadow with a bright caustic centre.
findings.fix: Lens: in the glass material's onBeforeCompile, replace `vec3 refractedRayExit = position + transmissionRay;` in THREE.ShaderChunk.transmission_pars_fragment with a two-refraction sphere trace. Use C = vec3(modelMatrix[3]) and R = thickness * modelScale.x (thickness = r). Refract t1 = refract(-v, n, 1/ior) at entry, Q = position + t1 * (-2.0 * dot(t1, position - C)), t2 = refract(t1, -normalize(Q - C), ior), then sample Q + t2 * 4R. Make the vane material transparent (opacity 1, drawn after the glass, glass depthWrite false) so the vane is not run through the lens mapping. Shadow: set cast:true on the glass with a customDepthMaterial that alpha-tests a 4x4 dither at about 35% coverage, so PCF gives a light shadow.

findings.problem: The studio's floor grain is a function of azimuth only (colGrain[x], line 443). So the mirror ball's lower half shows a fan of radial streaks converging on its contact point, like pumpkin meridians (r2-balls-r3-q-steel-ball c0/c1, -contact-steel-ball). A real table's grain is parallel lines, which a chrome ball shows as curves running across its lower half toward the left and right edges. The same fan shows faintly on the billiard and bowling balls.
findings.fix: In studio(), for rows below the horizon compute the floor point at unit height, zf = sin(az) / tan(-el) (az from +x toward +z), and use gm = 1 + grainW * smooth(4, 1, |zf|) * (0.7*noise3(zf*7, 0.5, 0) + 0.3*noise3(zf*19, 3.1, 0)) in place of colGrain[x]. The grain then runs along world x like the table's. It stays a one-off bake of about 1-2 ms.

findings.problem: The marbling is baked at 1024x512 over a 685 mm circumference (0.67 mm per texel). In a close orbit view about 10 cm from the ball the swirls and veins go visibly soft (r2-balls-r3-q-bowling-ball macro); real reactive-resin marbling has crisp veins.
findings.fix: Bake the colour map at 2048x1024 (the warp and field grids stay coarse, so only the per-pixel band/crest pass grows). Estimated +20-30 ms on the current 31 ms.

findings.problem: The chrome reflects only the baked studio, never its neighbours. In the lineup the big red beach ball and the bowling ball beside it do not appear in it (r2-balls-r3-q-steel-ball ctx).
findings.fix: web/view3d.js: after load or a layout change, render a 128 px CubeCamera at each metalness-1, roughness < 0.1 ball's centre (that ball hidden), set it as that mesh's envMap, and re-render only when the layout changes.

findings.problem: The wide camera's vertical FOV is 54.9° (about 69° horizontal), so balls near the frame's left and right edges are drawn about 15-20% wider than tall, like eggs (r2-balls-r3-wide: superball, plastic ball and tennis ball at the left). A product photo uses a longer lens.
findings.fix: web/view3d.js: frame the wide camera with a 30-35° vertical FOV and pull it back to fit the same stage.

findings.problem: Resting balls are drawn 0.86-0.94 mm above the tabletop (the engine's contact skin). The view lowers only resting slabs and polygons. On the 16 mm marble and the 25 mm steel ball the gap is 4-7% of the diameter and shows in low views (r2-balls-r3-contact-*).
findings.fix: web/view3d.js: apply the same resting-gap rule to round bodies. A ball whose lowest point is under 2 mm above the tabletop or a static slab, and which is not moving away from it, is drawn lowered by that gap.

costs: superball: 17.9 ms cold (studio pre-baked, min of 3 fresh iframes; runs 17.9/17.9/19.5) / 16,128 triangles, 1 mesh
baseball: 102.4 ms / 21,984, 2 meshes; every new size re-bakes its maps: 106-117 ms per resize step (see the major finding)
steel-ball: 16.8 ms including the shared studio HDR bake / 16,128, 1 mesh
Load average was about 6 during the timings. Resize cost of the other balls: beach 2-4 ms, bowling about 1 ms, marble about 1 ms, tennis under 1 ms, basketball about 0 ms.

needs_elsewhere: web/thumbs3d.js render() (drawPreview3D): the glass marble card is blank because the renderer has alpha:true with a fully transparent clear colour, so the transmission buffer behind the glass is empty. When any preview solid's look has transmission > 0 (looks[s.look]?.transmission), set scene.background = new THREE.Color(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--card').trim() || '#f4f2ee') for that shot and clear it afterwards. Alternatively always add a seamless backdrop plane behind the item. Other groups' glass blocks have the same problem.

web/view3d.js (steel ball and any metalness-1 ball with roughness under 0.1): after a load or layout change, render a 128 px CubeCamera of the real scene at the ball with the ball hidden, and set it as that mesh's material.envMap. This would put the real table and neighbouring balls in the chrome. I added grain to the studio floor as a stopgap only.

web/thumbs3d.js, init()/render(): transmissive materials have nothing to refract on the transparent clear, so the glass-marble card comes out a white disc (any glass block from other groups too). Before renderer.render(scene, camera) in shoot(), when any built material in the group has transmission > 0 (traverse the group and check o.material.transmission), set scene.background = new THREE.Color(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--card').trim() || '#f4f2ee') (the card's own surface colour; my thumbs page used #f3f1ec) and restore scene.background = null right after the render, or always add a seamless backdrop plane behind the item. Setting the colour alone would leave the card's own background showing for opaque balls, so apply it only when a transmissive material is present.

web/view3d.js: mirror-chrome balls (metalness 1, roughness < 0.1: the steel ball) reflect only the baked studio. After load or a layout change, render a 128 px CubeCamera of the scene at each such ball's centre (the ball itself hidden) and set it as that mesh's material.envMap, re-rendering only when the layout changes. That puts the neighbouring beach and bowling balls into the chrome.

final.verdict: Round 3 does not pass. I checked every item: on the table at normal distance, in close-ups from two angles, against the physics outline drawn over an orthographic front view, on its catalog card, and in its scenarios. At default sizes all 12 items match their outlines (model minus outline is +0.75 mm on each side, the skin; the wedge sticks out 0.75 mm and its tip falls 0.73 mm short; z is exact). They also sit on the table correctly; the view raises every resting item by 1.0 mm. All 12 build within budget. The wedge physics is done right: a counter-clockwise right triangle, 0.70 kg (700 kg/m³ × 0.01 m² × 0.1 m), size handle on the top corner of the back, rotate handle. It works as a ramp both ways: a golf ball rolls down the slope and off, and a ball rolling across the table rides up from the tip and is launched. At default sizes the wood, brick, steel, foam, cardboard, domino, domino row and ice-cube models now look like the real things. Two problems inside the group are still major. (1) Resizing the cardboard box, which its own size handle does, smears the texture: on any face bigger than the 30×20 cm print tile the edge pixels stretch into streaks around a pasted-on patch, and on a smaller box the print is cut into pieces. (2) The new wedge in the ice material is a plain, nearly invisible clear prism with a dark smudge. Its texture coordinates are all one point, so the frost never shows, and it has none of the ice cube's frost layer, milky body or cloudy core. Minor problems: the log's bark close up (rounded loop shapes and sawtooth edges along the furrows), bark that stretches with the log's diameter, the wall's glue lines showing as dotted lines, wood grain visibly repeating on large faces, magnified end grain on large wedges, and two flat-looking catalog cards. Checks: test_rg PASS (worst difference 0.0, 'Ball 2 lands in the box' ok). test_catalog passes all 12 blocks types. Through /api/simulate: car-ramp-dominoes 7 of 7 dominoes fall, pendulum-dominoes 7 of 7, rube-goldberg goal met with 7 of 7, wrecking-ball moves all 5 bricks (5 mm threshold; the fixer reported brick 1 does not move), plinko runs with no warnings. The walls in rube-goldberg and plinko are invisible in 3D, so the wall model only shows when a user adds one. Every page I loaded had an empty console. Shots are in web/dev/shots/r2-blocks-r3-*.png. My dev page is web/dev/r2-review-blocks.html, used unchanged. I edited no project files, and my own headless Chromium is closed.

findings.problem: Resizing breaks the box texture. kraftTile() bakes the side, end and top with wrap:false at a fixed 0.30×0.20 m (side and top) and 0.20×0.20 m (end), centred on each face. At 600×400×400 mm the edge pixels stretch into a plaid of streaks around a pasted-on printed patch, and the corners are flat colour with no flutes. This is visible at 1.4 m: r2-blocks-r3-boxes, boxbig-front, boxbig-top. At 100×60×80 mm the print is cut to fragments ('G CO.', half an arrow): r2-blocks-r3-boxsmall. The box's size handle makes this happen on every resize.
findings.fix: In cardboardBox(), separate the cardboard from the print. (1) Bake one plain, tileable kraft texture with wrap:true (flutes and fibres only, no print), e.g. 0.2×0.2 m at 2 px/mm with a whole number of flutes. Map it on all six faces at real size through the softBox tile entries so it repeats instead of stretching. (2) Draw the print (sidePrint/endPrint) as separate decal meshes: a PlaneGeometry 0.05 mm outside each printed face, with polygonOffset as on the seam, and an ink-only canvas texture (alpha mask, 0-alpha border, clamped, transparent, depthWrite false). Size each decal to the print's real size times s = min(1, (faceW − 0.02)/0.30, (faceH − 0.02)/0.20), centred, and leave it out when s < 0.3. A 300×200×200 mm box must look the same as now. Cost: two or three extra quads per box.

findings.problem: The ice wedge is a uniform, nearly invisible clear prism with a dark smudge, unlike the ice cube next to it (r2-blocks-r3-var-ice; 6th item in var-wide and var-a). Cause: wedgeModel's ice branch calls prismGeo(..., () => [0.5, 0.5]), so every vertex has the same texture coordinate and the shell's frost roughness map samples one pixel. The branch also builds only iceShell(), without the frost layer, milky body, contact shadow or cloudy core that blockIce() adds.
findings.fix: In the ice branch of wedgeModel(): (1) give prismGeo real texture coordinates (lids ((x−x0)/bw, (y−y0)/bh); sides (arc/perimeter, (z+depth/2)/depth)) so frostTex's edge term whitens the edges. (2) Add the cube's layers made from the outline: a frost layer (prismGeo of roundedOutline(pts, SKIN_M + 0.0001, r), material 'ice-frost' with alphaMap F.roughMap, renderOrder 4), an 'ice-milk' inner prism (outline shrunk by 0.8 mm), and the 'ice-contact' plane under the base (userData.iceShell = true). (3) Add a cloudy core: blockIce's blob set scaled by the triangle's inradius, centred low on the centroid (x0 + 2bw/3, y0 + bh/3), with the halo and a few bubbles. Then call iceFinish(). Keep every part inside the outline and z within ±d/2. Expect about 3k triangles and under 40 ms.

findings.problem: Close up (17–35 cm) the bark still looks sculpted rather than like oak. The fissures are the 0.5 contour lines of smooth noise, so they form rounded lobes and closed loops instead of long, deep, roughly parallel furrows (r2-blocks-r3-log2, log-side, log-top). The furrow wall is about one texel wide (f1 = 1 − sstep(0, 0.03, da)), so the normal map draws a zipper of sawtooth teeth along many fissure edges (crop of log-top). The furrows are not dark enough for their depth.
findings.fix: In barkDepth(): widen the walls to at least 2.5 texels: f1 = 1 − sstep(0, 0.07, da), plate = 0.92 + 0.08·sstep(0.07, 0.18, da). Make the fissures run lengthwise: a ridged term (1 − |2·pnS(40, 1)(u + warp, v) − 1|) with the warp mostly in u, min-combined with the current two contour sets. In bake(), blur the height field 1 px (3×3 box) before computing the normals when normal ≥ 6. In barkTex(), darken the furrow floor to about [28, 20, 16] for d < 0.25. Bump the bake key to bark6.

findings.problem: The bark tile always covers exactly one turn around the log (uv.x = t), so the bark scales with the diameter. A 300 mm log gets plates 2.5× too wide, with long flat blotches (r2-blocks-r3-logbig), and a 40 mm stick gets squeezed ones.
findings.fix: In logGeometry(), repeat the tile k = max(1, round(R / 0.06)) times around the log (uv.x = t·k; barkDepth is already periodic in u). rAt() must sample the same k·t, so the geometry's furrows stay lined up with the normal map. The default 120 mm log does not change.

findings.problem: Between the three staves, the dark 'wall-glue' box shows through the V-grooves made by each stave's 0.6 mm rounded inner edges. At normal viewing distance this aliases into dotted, dashed lines that read as stitching (r2-blocks-r3-wall, wide-shot crop). A real edge-glued panel is sanded flush, so its joints show only as a change of tone and grain. The rube-goldberg and plinko walls are invisible in 3D, so only a wall the user adds shows this.
findings.fix: In wallPanel(): remove the glue box and the inner roundings. Build the board as one softBox (W, H, d, r = 0.6 mm), so it is one geometry with no grooves. Show the staves as two thin seam strips per broad face: PlaneGeometry 0.35 mm × H at z = ±d/6, colour #6b4a2e at opacity 0.3, polygonOffset, depthWrite false. Use the same strips on the top and bottom end grain. Optionally tint each third of the face slightly differently with variantOf (±4%).

findings.problem: The flat-sawn long-grain tile (LONG_T 0.48 × 0.12 m) repeats vertically, so a block face taller than about 0.13 m shows the same band of arches stacked 2–3 times (r2-blocks-r3-bigblk, 600×300×300 block). The wedge's end grain is magnified on large wedges: sc = max(0.6, bw/0.24, bh/0.12) gives 5× on a 1.2 × 0.3 m wedge, so rings come out 13 mm apart, pores 2–3 mm blobs, and the texture blurs to about 0.8 px/mm (r2-blocks-r3-bigw-z).
findings.fix: For faces taller than LONG_T[1], use the straight (rift-sawn) tile, or lazily bake a taller variant (0.48 × 0.24 m at the same px/mm, key wood-long3-tall). In wedgeModel, cap sc at 1.5. Beyond that, use MirroredRepeatWrapping on a mirrored copy of endWide (mirrored ring arcs still read as plank end), or bake woodEndWide per size class (×2 tile, ≥ 1.9 px/mm) keyed by class.

findings.problem: On the catalog card both cubes are flat mid-grey with almost no studio reflections, and the engraved '1 kg' and '5 kg' are barely legible (r2-blocks-r3-thumbs). In the scene they look right.
findings.fix: graded() already detects a card when the mesh has no solidId (the uTable test in onBeforeRender). Use the same test to raise envMapIntensity by about 1.6× and lower roughness by 0.05 on the steel material for cards only. Keep the scene values unchanged.

findings.problem: The card's stand-in reads as a milky frosted box with a grey lower half, not as clear refracting ice (r2-blocks-r3-thumbs, thumbsz). The grey comes from the dark lower half of the card's environment and the empty transparent background.
findings.fix: web/thumbs3d.js: for transmissive items (ice-cube, the glass and ice variants, the ice wedge), photograph over an opaque pale studio backdrop (a soft #e6ecf0 floor plane or clear colour), so the real transmissive shell has something to refract and the stand-in is not needed. In the group meanwhile, FADE_STAND could add a whitening term to faces whose world normal points down (mix toward #eef6fb by 0.5·clamp(−n.y, 0, 1)).

costs: wooden-block: 79-85 ms cold (one first-page outlier at 100), 972 tris, 1 mesh / 1 geometry
brick: 74-75 ms (one first-page outlier at 191 that did not repeat in 5 reruns), 22,436 tris, 1/1
domino-row (7 tiles): 73-75 ms, 4,116 tris, 7 meshes / 7 geometries (sizes differ)

When any preview solid's look has transmission > 0 (ice, glass), add for that shot an opaque studio sweep behind the item (a PlaneGeometry backdrop plus floor, light-grey gradient #e9ecef to #c9ced4, MeshStandardMaterial roughness 1), keeping the clear alpha. Once that exists the stand-in in blocks.js is still harmless (it only shows when no mesh has a solidId).

final.verdict:
Round 3 does not pass yet. Two major problems can still be fixed inside the group's own files:
(1) The basket model ignores bottom_ratio. At ratio below 1 the drawn wicker walls stay straight while the collision walls slant in, so balls bounce off thin air inside the drawn basket.
(2) ice-sheet and glass-sheet default to legs:false. A raised or tilted sheet, which is the item's main use as a slide, floats in mid-air with nothing under it.

The round-2 fixes hold up when I looked at them:
- The dark smudge under the ice is gone.
- Carpet now reads as cut-pile velour.
- The Newton's cradle base is 'dark wood'.
- Peg-board is down from about 206k to 11.5k triangles: 52 pegs plus 52 bore rings as InstancedMesh, and 30.4k at 20x20.
- Bucket and basket at extreme sizes are within budget.

Every item builds cold in 99 ms or less (hinged-gate is the worst) and stays at or under 27.1k triangles at default props.

Tests and scenarios:
- test_rg.py passes and test_catalog.py passes 139 of 139.
- All scenarios that use the group's items keep their goals: rube-goldberg, conveyor (3/3), spring-launch, plinko, newtons-cradle and both domino scenarios, with 0 warnings.

Open majors in other files, unchanged:
- The render-only mounts float in the air: the pendulum and gate wall plates, the peg and bumper plates, and the plinko board, which hangs 0.17 to 0.97 m above the table with no support. This needs the view3d.js stand hint.
- The ice and glass catalog cards are blank white (thumbs3d.js).

The round-1 review file named in the task (scratchpad/round1/surfaces.json) does not exist, so I judged everything from fresh pictures. My dev page is web/dev/r2-review-surfaces.html (round-3 helpers added: doItem, scn, bbox2). Pictures are in web/dev/shots/r3-surfaces-*.png.

findings.problem: web/models/containers.js basket() builds straight walls W wide from floor to rim and ignores P.bottom_ratio, but the physics walls slant (Wb = W*bottom_ratio at the floor). At bottom_ratio 0.6 the drawn wall is 90.5 mm outside the floor slab on each side, and at 0.3 it is 158 mm outside (bbox2; outline r3-surfaces-basket-taper-sheet, r3-surfaces-basket-r03-sheet). Test: basket at ratio 0.3, tennis ball dropped 0.15 m left of centre from 0.4 m. It hits bk/left at t=0.223 s with its bottom 124 mm above the drawn floor, bouncing off empty air inside the drawn wicker box. Cup and bucket do follow the taper.
findings.fix: In basket(), set Wb = W*P.bottom_ratio and make the wall geometry a function of height. For each plan-path vertex (x, z) at height y, use x' = x*s(y) with s(y) = (Wb + (W-Wb)*y/H)/W. Optionally scale z the same way, which stays inside ±D/2. Tilt the wall normals by atan((W-Wb)/(2H)), build the floor weave at Wb (x D or D*s(0)), keep the rim at W, and add bottom_ratio to `key`. Check with the ortho outline at ratios 0.3, 0.6 and 1.0: the lower wall corners must sit within 1 mm of the slanted slabs. The triangle count is unchanged.

findings.problem: machines/catalog_items.py _surface(..., legs=False) for ice-sheet (about line 329) and glass-sheet (about line 331). Used as a slide (raised and tilted, as the description suggests), the sheet floats in mid-air with no support (r3-surfaces-ice-sheet-ramp-sheet). Plank, steel-beam, rubber, carpet and concrete all default to legs. The help text says legs are off 'they would show through it', but legs showing through clear ice or glass is what a real glass shelf looks like (r3-surfaces-ice-sheet-ramp-legs-sheet and glass-sheet-ramp-legs-sheet look right).
findings.fix: Default legs=True for both and drop the 'off for a clear pane' help wording. view3d draws no leg for an end under 3 cm above its support, so a sheet lying on the table is unchanged; plank (legs on) resting on the table shows none. This is a render hint only, with no physics change. Reload the catalog.

findings.problem: The render-only mounts still float. The pendulum and gate wall plates hang in mid-air (pendulum-dominoes scenario: the plate floats about 0.45 m above the table in front of nothing). The peg and bumper backing plates float. findings.problem:
The ends of the shoe are torn and creased, at the heel back and at the toe tip. The sole, midsole, orange stripe and heel cup are built as one closed shape stretched along the shoe's length (x), capped with a flat fan at each end. Where the plan narrows to a point (heel radius 37 mm, toe tip 3 mm wide), the cross-sections shrink to slivers.
- Heel (r2-everyday-silhouettes-r3-sneaker-rear, sneaker-heel-crop): a vertical crease down the back centre, light and dark faceted patches on the white cup, and a ragged step where the cup meets the midsole about 25 mm up. The orange stripe kinks at the back corner. The lower-heel kink is visible even at normal distance (sneaker-b).
- Toe (sneaker-front, sneaker-toe-crop, and in the background of egg-a): the orange stripe breaks into separate pieces with a V-notch at the toe front, and the midsole top edge has a notch and crack at the centre.
Both defects are at the most-looked-at points of a shoe.
findings.fix:
In web/models/everyday-b-shoe.js:
(1) Build the orange stripe as one closed band() tube (the function already exists, with closed:true) along the plan perimeter. Sample points (x, ym(x), ±(soleHalf(x,±1) - 0.2)) round the plan, using a semicircle of radius 37 at the heel and the WTAB toe curve at the front. Do not use an x-loft of rings for the stripe.
(2) For the outsole, midsole and white heel cup, stop the x-loft where the plan half-width is at least about 10 mm (about x > 6 at the heel, x < 290 at the toe). Close each end with a cap swept round the plan's end curve. Parametrise it by perimeter angle θ about a vertical axis at the end (heel: centre (37, *, 0), θ from -90 to 90 degrees). At each θ, reuse the same vertical section heights as the last ring: bottom chord, foam top, stripe height and cup top, evaluated at that perimeter point's x. Use the same ring vertex count, so the cap stitches to the loft with no fan and no degenerate triangles.
(3) Remove the min(..., hi-3.6) clamp in ySole near x<5, which makes the step on the rounded back corner; the perimeter cap replaces it.
Then re-shoot the heel from directly behind and the toe from directly in front.

findings.problem: The shadows of the clear PET bottles and the glass jar still look like smeared sand or dirt in every close look: blotchy, random clumps of dark grain. See r2-everyday-silhouettes-r3-glass-jar-a/-b, jar-shadow-crop, bottle-shadow-crop and water-bottle-side-a. glassShadow() in web/models/everyday-b-lib.js dithers in the texture's UV space: a 4x4 Bayer tile repeated 512x256 times, so about 0.5 mm per tile on the jar. That is far finer than a shadow-map texel (the 4096 map over the scene is about 1 mm per texel or more). Each texel lands on an effectively random dither cell, and the soft shadow filter then smears that aliasing into blotches. In the default Wide view it is faint; in the Orbit or Follow camera, or any close look, it is obvious.
findings.fix: In everyday-b-lib.js glassShadow(), dither in shadow-map space instead of UV space. Give the proxy mesh a customDepthMaterial: new THREE.MeshDepthMaterial({depthPacking: THREE.RGBADepthPacking}) with onBeforeCompile replacing 'void main() {' with a bayer4(gl_FragCoord.xy) function (the 16 thresholds 0,8,2,10,12,4,14,6,3,11,1,9,15,7,13,5, each (v+0.5)/16) plus 'void main() { if (bayer4(gl_FragCoord.xy) >= density) discard;'. Give the proxy's own material no alphaMap (MeshBasicMaterial colorWrite:false, depthWrite:false). Cache one depth material per density in shadowMats. I applied exactly this live to the scene in my dev page; project files were not changed (r2-everyday-silhouettes-r3-shfix-before2 vs -after2). The jar's shadow turns from blotchy grain into an even, lighter grey, with only a faint regular dot grid in an extreme close-up. A 2x2 ordered pattern at density 0.25 or 0.5 removes even that under the soft shadow filter.

findings.problem: In the catalog card thumbnails, the glass jar renders as a solid opaque white jar and both bottles look milky white (r2-everyday-silhouettes-r3-thumbs). The thumbnail renderer in thumbs3d.js clears to transparent, with no scene.background. The transmission pass of the glass and PET materials therefore samples nothing, and the glass comes out white. My trial that set transmission to 0 for the card (glassfix=1) makes the jar read as clear glass.
findings.fix: In web/thumbs3d.js render(), before renderer.render, swap each mesh material that has transmission > 0 for a cached card-only clone: transmission 0, transparent true, opacity 0.14 + 0.5 × (1 - transmission), depthWrite false, envMapIntensity 1.2 so the edges keep their reflections. Restore the originals after the render. Handle array materials as well; my trial missed some of the bottle parts. Simpler alternative: set scene.background = new THREE.Color('#f4f4f2') (the card colour) while rendering a model that has transmission, so the transmission pass sees a backdrop.

findings.problem: In a close-up (r2-everyday-silhouettes-r3-c-mug-handle), the handle's lower root reads as a rounded knob stuck onto the wall, not a glazed fillet. The strap fattens mostly across its depth (rb +32 %) and only +20 % in the plane, and it enters the wall horizontally with no flare. The upper root is fine. Also, at a wide size (diameter 0.12, height 0.07, var-coffee-mug-wide) the handle stretches with the diameter and looks long and flat. Real mugs keep a hand-sized handle.
findings.fix: In everyday-b-bottles.js, near the ends (fl > 0) grow ra (in the plane) by up to 1.4 times: the arms are 10 mm tall, so a radius up to about 7 mm stays within the 2 mm allowance. Hold rb at 1.1 times or less. Add 2 or 3 centre-line points so the last 6 mm curve slightly toward the wall normal. Optional, in both mug_up and the model: scale the handle pieces uniformly by min(sx, sy) instead of sx and sy separately, keeping the arms' wall-side x tied to the wall.

findings.problem: The model (the true egg curve) sticks out of the 8-point physics outline by 1.1 to 1.6 mm along the four diagonal sides, and by 0.7 to 1.1 mm at the tips (window.silhouette, r2-everyday-silhouettes-r3-egg-ol). That is over the roughly 1 mm rule. The egg also rocks across eight flats instead of a curve.
findings.fix: In catalog_everyday.py build_egg, use 2 convex pieces: the upper and lower halves split along the long axis. That gives up to 14 outline points; place them on the egg curve with the chords straddling it, which keeps the error under about 0.4 mm. The upper half is welded to the lower half, which is the main solid, so no gap is needed. Keep the shares by area.

findings.problem: From normal 3/4 views (water-bottle-side-a/-b) the air bubble along the top cannot be seen; there is no visible water line. It only shows end-on. A real lying bottle shows a bright, flat waterline running its whole length.
findings.fix: Give the cut plane of the water a thin, slightly brighter meniscus edge (a narrow strip with higher roughness or a lighter tint along the cut's rim), or lower the cut plane to about 6 mm below the wall, so the flat surface catches the key light from above.

findings.problem: Each slider step rebuilds the whole shoe: a resize takes 63 ms the first time after a cold build, and 12 ms when warm. A drag stutters at roughly 16 fps. Cold builds are fine (126 ms first in a page, 28 ms when the JavaScript engine is already warmed up).
findings.fix: Cache the size-independent geometry, built in shoe millimetres, keyed on nothing, and apply the props as g.scale.set(W/0.3, H/0.11, D/0.105). The model is already built in shoe millimetres and then scaled, so a resize only needs a new scale.

findings.problem: The mug's catalog card shows a dotted, dashed dark line along the inner rim lip (shadow acne). The main view does not show it.
findings.fix: In web/thumbs3d.js init(), set key.shadow.normalBias = 0.002 (keep bias -0.0004), or raise the bias to -0.001.

needs_elsewhere: web/thumbs3d.js, init(): use renderer.setClearColor(0xf4f4f2, 1) (the card colour) in place of (0x000000, 0). The glass-jar card is an opaque white tub and both bottle cards are milky because transmissive materials have nothing to refract on a transparent clear colour (see r2-es-fx-thumbs1.png; in the 3D scene they are clear). Alternative: in render(), before shoot(group), swap each mesh whose material.transmission > 0 for a cached clone {transmission: 0, transparent: true, opacity: 0.16, depthWrite: false} and restore it afterwards.

machines/catalog_everyday.py, the chopstick entry (everyday-a group, not touched): at its minimum size the engine refuses it (height/depth min 0.0012 gives a side of exactly 0.50 mm: 'polygon has a side 0.50 mm long'); add mins={'height': 0.0016, 'depth': 0.0016} to _box('chopstick', ...). machines/test_everyday.py prints this as a warning ('extremes (not this group's type)') until it is fixed; it does not fail the run.

tooling/src/sim/physics.ts, engine: an interim fix for sibling creep was applied in the catalog, but the cause is in the engine. The loop that creates each solid's WeldJoint (new WeldJoint({}, to, body, ...)) joins every child to its parent, and planck skips contacts only between the two bodies a weld joins. Siblings welded to the same main solid still collide through the 1 mm polygon skin (polygonRadius 0.01 in planck units, a 1.5 mm rest gap), so an overlapping or touching pair pushes against its welds for ever. Change: give every solid of one welded compound (all solids joined through parent links with no pivot) the same negative filterGroupIndex, unique per compound (for example -(compound index + 1)), in the createFixture userData/filter for each polygon, slab or ball. Better: build a welded compound as a single body with one fixture per solid. That would also take the weld-chain landing error away (a duck with every piece welded to a piece that is not the one that lands tipped to -62 degrees on a 20 cm drop). After that, the 1.2 mm gaps in _apart/gap= can be removed.

web/thumbs3d.js, init(): replace renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0) with renderer.setClearColor(0xf4f4f2, 1) (the card colour). Transmissive materials have nothing to refract against a transparent clear, which is why the glass jar shows as an opaque white tub and the bottles as milky white. Alternative: in render(), just before shoot(group), swap every mesh whose material.transmission > 0 for a cached clone with {transmission: 0, transparent: true, opacity: 0.16, depthWrite: false} and put the original back after.

web/thumbs3d.js: draw the card with antialias: true or 2x supersampling and premultiplied alpha (or onto the opaque card-colour clear above), so the dotted dark fringe along the thumbnail silhouettes goes away.

final.verdict:
This round does not pass. Two major problems remain that can be fixed inside the group's own files. Most of the models now look right up close and match their physics outlines; I checked the side outlines in front views and the bbox against each outline. The items checked closely: the launcher, bounce pad, bumper (wood, steel and rubber plates), spring gate hinge, catapult clevis post with its 70° stop visible, rope-pendulum bob and screw eye, wrecking-ball jib and lug, swing, chain links and clevis blocks, round pail and bail. Tests: test_mechanisms 29/29 PASS, test_rg PASS, rw-validate-p2 ALL PASS. Scenarios: atwood, spring-launch, trampoline and rube-goldberg hold; in wrecking-ball, brick 1 still never moves (the scenario file is outside the group). Every item meets the build budget: at most 34 ms cold and 22.6k triangles at defaults, 28.6k at extreme props.

The two majors:
(1) The trampoline mat bakes a new 2048 px texture for every width or depth value. I measured +2 GPU textures per slider step that are never freed, about 17 MB each.
(2) A hanging chain set to varnished hardwood is still drawn as zinc steel.

The biggest visual faults left are outside the group's files:
- view3d.js draws one spring per trampoline end instead of the 10 rows the catalog asks for.
- view3d.js places and draws the Atwood and pulley-lift wheels wrongly.
- thumbs3d.js cards have no pulley wheels or ropes, a thin brown line instead of the wrecking-ball chain, and grey hanger shadows in the middle of the picture.

findings.problem: mechanisms-tramp.js bakes the mat's top texture at 2048 x max(512, 2048*d/w) px under the key tramMatTop|w|d, and the weave normal map under tramWeave|rep (rep comes from w and d). So every mat width or depth makes new textures, and nothing evicts them (models3d.js trims only geometries). Measured with renderer.info.memory.textures over 20 width steps via /api/layout + view.load: 10 -> 50 textures, +2 per step, never freed. The map is about 12.6 MB, about 17 MB with mipmaps, per step, so dragging the Mat width slider across its range can use gigabytes of GPU memory. This breaks the rule to bake at the resolution needed and reuse bakes.
findings.fix: Make the mat's textures independent of its size. (a) Bake one tileable 256x256 tile of the woven tape lines plus a fixed-key weave normal map. Give the mat's top face true-scale UVs in metres (rbox with uv: true, grain 0, tu = tv = 0.06), or set repeat on a texture.clone() that shares the image source. (b) Draw the 30 mm webbing hem and its two stitch lines as four thin strip meshes, 0.2 mm above the top face. Use one tileable webbing+stitch texture (e.g. 512x64 for a 6 cm run) with UVs in metres along each strip. (c) Draw the centre ring and cross as a small decal plane with one fixed 256x256 texture. After this, no texture key contains w or d.

findings.problem: linkModel in mechanisms-ropes.js always uses L.zinc(). The catalog offers 'varnished hardwood' (and 'aluminium') for the chain, and the link solids then carry look 'wood'. Seen in r2-mechanisms-v3-mat-woodchain.png: a hardwood chain, about 8x lighter in the physics, is drawn as polished steel, so what the user sees disagrees with what the chain is.
findings.fix: In linkModel, pick the material from the solid's look: const sk = L.skin(ctx). Use L.zinc() for steel, L.alu() for aluminium, and a wood material for wood: L.woodSet(ctx.color, seedOf(ctx)).side, with the bar geometry's UVs scaled to true size so the grain runs along each link (u = x / 0.24 m). Alternatively, remove 'varnished hardwood' from _has(...) in catalog_mechanisms.py's hanging-chain registration, but only if saved scenes using it can be migrated.

findings.problem: stamp() in mechanisms-parts.js bakes a 768x256 ink map plus a 768x256 bump map per text and per band height (key `${text}|${f5(bandH)}`). Every weight value is a new pair that is never freed. Measured: 10 hanging-spring weight steps -> +20 GPU textures (57 -> 77), about 2 MB per step.
findings.fix: Key the stamp by text only and make the band's aspect fixed (3:1), so bandH only scales the patch geometry. Bake at 384x128, which is enough for a 1 cm label. Or draw the value from one shared digit atlas (0-9, '.', ' ', 'g', 'k') with one quad per character, so no new textures are made at all.

findings.problem: (1) build_hanging still anchors the spring at the hanger's underside, anchorA=(0, -0.006). The coil's end runs up through the brass screw-eye ring into its shank instead of hooking on the ring, which is SCREW_EYE = 3 mm lower. (2) _spring caps the coil count at 24, so a 0.3 m lab spring is drawn with a 12.5 mm pitch at rest. Its open coils read as a compression spring; a Hooke's-law lab spring is a close-wound extension spring.
findings.fix: Set anchorA=(0, -0.006 - SCREW_EYE) and place the weight at y = -(rest + stretch) - s/2 - SCREW_EYE, so the rest length, stretch and period stay exact; test_mechanisms's period check is unchanged. Pass coils=max(24, round(rest/0.004)), which gives 75 turns at 0.3 m (the view then needs fewer segments per turn: see the trampoline spring request).

findings.problem: ballSkin() treats 'modeling clay' as 'other' and uses L.plasticMat (roughness 0.38, clearcoat 0.3). The clay bob renders as a glossy green plastic ball with sharp highlights (r2-mechanisms-v3-mat-claybob.png), but modeling clay is dead matte.
findings.fix: Add a branch: if (look === 'clay') use L.MAT(`clay|${ctx.color}`, {color: L.rich(ctx.color), roughness: 0.9, metalness: 0, normalMap: L.normalTex('clayLumps', 128, 128, (x,y) => L.vnoise(x/16, y/16, 3, 8), {strength: 0.8}), normalScale: (0.4, 0.4)}), with no clearcoat.

findings.problem: (1) The brass funnel eyelets stand 4.8 mm above the seat's top (bbox seat y +4.80 mm), beyond the 2 mm rule. A ball resting on the seat beside a rope would sink into them visually. (2) The stopper knot is buried in the plank and covered by a flat black disc on the underside, which reads as a painted dot with a sliver of rope in it (r2-mechanisms-v3-sw-knot3.png), not a counterbore. (3) At ±30° the model's vertical 4 mm rope stub shows beside the view's angled rope inside the funnel.
findings.fix: Make the eyelet a flanged grommet: a lathe flange 0.8 mm thick and at most 1.5 mm proud, with its neck going down into the hole. End the rope stub at yTop = h/2 - 0.001, inside the hole. Model the counterbore as a real recess: a CylinderGeometry(0.0072, 0.0072, 0.004, 28, 1, true) with side BackSide in holeDark, 4 mm up from the underside, plus a dark annulus at its top. Seat the knot in it so the knot's lowest point is 0.5-1.5 mm below the plank.

findings.problem: The end-grain tile (te = 0.1 m) does not tile seamlessly. On an end face 10 cm or longer, such as the bumper wall's 3 x 10 cm top, the growth rings jump along a straight line where the tile wraps (r2-mechanisms-v3-sb-walltop.png).
findings.fix: In uvBox and woodGeo, compute the end face's two extents for each geometry and use teFace = max(te, 1.05 * the larger extent) for that face's UVs, so no end face ever wraps. Alternatively, use MirroredRepeatWrapping on the endTex textures.

findings.problem: The slot is a box 2r*0.78 long, centred 0.05 mm above the dome's crown. The dome is only 0.5r tall, so the box's ends float about 0.7 mm clear of the head. Close up, every base and hanger screw shows a raised dark blade, not a cut slot (r2-mechanisms-v3-sl-screw.png).
findings.fix: Build the dome head as two half-domes (LatheGeometry with phiLength = PI, at phiStart 0 and PI), moved ±0.11r apart across the slot. Fill the gap between them with a dark box from y = 0 to 0.5r - 0.4 mm. Cache the result under mscrewSlot|r.

findings.problem: The arm overshoots to -44.6° and hits the stop at 0.577 s at 1.7 m/s, then rests at -43.3°: inside Box2D's 2° angular slop on the -45° limit. So the real sweep is 68.3°, not 70°. A 2.7-4.2 mm gap stays between the arm's underside and the rubber cap, visible close up (r2-mechanisms-v3-sc-ol-after.png).
findings.fix: In build_catapult, place the stop for the resting angle rather than the limit. Compute y_top with th_rest = th + 1.7*D2R and a 0.5 mm gap instead of 1.5 mm, so the arm visibly sits on the cap. Re-check test_mechanisms's catapult throw (currently 350 cm right, 80 cm up).

findings.problem: The bail's ends go straight down into plain aluminium sleeves at the rim. The riveted ears 12 mm below the rim are not connected to anything. On a real pail the bail hooks through a hole in each ear.
findings.fix: Turn the ear into the bail's pivot. Raise the ear so its top meets the rim bead, and add a pierced boss on it at the arc's end: a small torus, minor radius 0.6 mm, around the wire end. Drop the separate sleeve. Keep everything within 1.3 mm of the wall.

findings.problem: The hazard-stripe paint is baked at 128x128 and stretched over about 6 cm of the paddle tip. Close up, the diagonal stripe edges are stepped and soft (r2-mechanisms-v3-ms-tip.png).
findings.fix: Bake spinnerHazard at 256x256. It is one bake shared by every paddle, so it adds under 1 ms and about 0.3 MB.

findings.problem: At extreme props (30 links, 3 m chain, 2 m span, 3 mm thickness), the link cap stretches the pitch. The chain is drawn as long paperclip links about 3x normal length (r2-mechanisms-v3-hcx-cu.png). The triangle budget is met (22.1k).
findings.fix: When the cap is reached, keep normal link proportions. Draw the excess length with 3x4-segment links before lengthening the pitch: about 60 triangles per link, so about 330 links fit in 20k. Allow the pitch to grow only past that.

findings.problem: view3d.js buildSpring draws one coil per end at z = 0. The catalog sends render {rows: 10}, and the frames and mat draw 10 hooks and 10 V-rings per side, 9 of which have no spring (r2-mechanisms-v3-tr-cu1.png). A trampoline's defining detail, its row of springs, is missing.
findings.fix: In view3d.js buildSpring: when j.render?.rows = n > 1, draw n coils with the same x-y anchors at z_k = -d/2 + (k + 0.5)*d/n, where d is the depth of j.a's body (the mat), as one InstancedMesh of the shared coil geometry. When turns > 24, use about 10 segments per turn instead of 18x8, so 37 turns is about 6k triangles instead of 10.6k.

findings.problem: view3d.js buildPulley has four problems: (1) wheel centres sit at groundA/B, so the vertical runs hang one wheel radius outboard of the bodies (the ropes slant); (2) an Atwood machine gets two wheels instead of one; (3) the bracket plate passes behind the bar and its eye sticks up through the bar's top; (4) the wheels have flat faces with a dark '+' and look like toys (r2-mechanisms-v3-at-c1.png).
findings.fix: view3d.js: put wheel A at groundA.x + wheelRadius and wheel B at groundB.x - wheelRadius. When j.render?.wheel === 'single', draw one wheel of radius |GB-GA|/2 at the midpoint. Hang the bracket below the bar (plate top at or below G.y + wheelRadius + 0.006, no eye above the bar). Give the wheels a hub and spokes or a recessed web. Then the group sets wheelRadius = d/2 and render={'wheel':'single'} in build_atwood and build_lift.

findings.problem: Catalog cards (r2-mechanisms-v3-thumbs.png). Atwood and pulley-lift show a bar and tiny weights floating, with no wheels or ropes, so they are unrecognisable. The wrecking-ball chain is a thin brown line. Seven cards show the static hanger's shadow as a grey card in mid-picture. The motor spinner shows no motor.
findings.fix: In thumbs3d.js: for j.kind === 'pulley', draw wheels (CylinderGeometry, r = j.wheelRadius, 12 mm thick, steel, axis z) at groundA/B and the rope runs. For a rope with render.style 'chain', draw steel links or a steel line of radius 0.75*thickness. Frame the card on the moving parts. Only let solids whose lowest point is within 5 cm of the card's floor cast shadows. Draw the motor can and shaft for a pivot with a motor.

findings.problem: In web/scenarios/wrecking-ball.json the bottom brick never moves. final.verdict:
Round 3: I checked all 8 vehicle items myself on a table in my own page (web/dev/r2-review-vehicles.html, shots web/dev/shots/r2-vehicles-rv3-*.png, downscaled copies in scratchpad/rv3v/). For each I took a wide context shot, two or more close-ups and a front view with the physics outlines drawn over it. I also checked material variants, extreme props and the car-ramp-dominoes scenario. None of the remaining problems is major and fixable inside the group.

What I confirmed:
- Every item rests on the table with no floating or sinking (wheels sit 0.5 mm high, the engine's contact skin) and stays level.
- Every model fills its physics outline. CHECK flags appear on the toy-car and motor-car mirrors, the truck's front wheel-arch meshes at an extreme size, and the skateboard hangers. Each of these lies inside a neighbouring solid's outline (the cabin's or the wheels').
- All 8 catalog cards render, the Cart included (NaN bug fixed), with no console warnings.
- The truck windscreen is one pane. The wooden wheel face is crisp, with no rim seam. The skateboard tip edge is continuous. The motor-car quarter window is a small triangle with a body-colour panel and no longer reads as a fin.
- test_rg.py: PASS. test_mechanisms.py: 29 of 29 pass.
- car-ramp-dominoes still reaches its outcome: the car tops 1.8 m/s and 7 of 7 dominoes fall.
- Triangle counts are under budget: truck 34.2k of 46k, motor-car 25.5k of 34k, toy-car 24.7k of 32k. Cold builds are all under 150 ms, though the first-load numbers for the motor-car (131 ms) and truck (126 ms) are close to the limit.

What remains:
- **Paint looks washed out (major, outside the group).** Yellow #ffc400 renders cream or khaki (216,188,121). Darker base colours, clearcoat 0 and lower env intensity all barely change it. Switching the renderer to NeutralToneMapping gives a true yellow (247,192,65) and true red wheels (side-by-side in scratchpad/rv3v/tm-compare.png).
- **Small fixes inside the group (minor):** the truck's wipers point different ways, the toy car's rear door is too short, and the motor car's fender tops show as thin edges up close.
- **Catalog cards (minor, outside the group):** every vehicle card is shot from the rear quarter.

findings.problem: The paint loses its saturation in the 3D view. Truck #ffc400 renders as cream/khaki (216,188,121) instead of a toy-truck yellow. The red steel wheels look brick, the toy car coral, the motor car pale. I tested it at runtime in my page. Base colours from #ffc400 down to #c88a00 all render (218,191,126) to (200,160,97). Clearcoat 0, roughness 0.5 and envMapIntensity 0.4 change nothing. The cause is the renderer's AgX tone mapping (toneMapping 6, exposure 1) with the 4.0 key DirectionalLight, not the model.
findings.fix: web/view3d.js (3D-view agent): set renderer.toneMapping = THREE.NeutralToneMapping (Khronos PBR Neutral, made for product-photo colour), keep outputColorSpace sRGB, and drop toneMappingExposure to about 0.85-0.9 so the wall and table do not brighten. Tested at runtime: the truck cab becomes (247,192,65), a true yellow, and the wheels become red (scratchpad/rv3v/tm-compare.png, shots r2-vehicles-rv3-tm-agx-fq.png / -tm-neutral-fq.png).
